=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Positions and Disclosure Letter

## Overall view

The Seller's package is not a fair and balanced starting point for Wattlebridge. It combines a low liability cap, broad general disclosure of the data room, an anti-sandbagging clause, and deferred treatment of known problems. Together these would leave Wattlebridge carrying most of the identified risks, roughly AUD 4.1m of quantified items plus an unquantified privacy exposure and Bluefen revenue dependence (about AUD 3.6m a year), while the Seller's total warranty exposure is capped at AUD 4.8m.

Several items are not warranty issues at all. They are known, specific problems that should be dealt with through price, conditions precedent, funds-flow deductions and special indemnities, not through the general warranty regime.

*Note: I have not verified statutory references or current rates. Confirm them with NSW counsel and tax advisers before relying on them. Some points, especially on the privacy timeline, are time-critical.*

---

## Issues, by priority

### 1. Privacy/export incident (DD-006): most urgent

- The Seller describes this as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material," but the record is unresolved. About 1,240 records, including names and activity timestamps, went to an unintended external address. It is not known whether anyone accessed the file, and the scope is unconfirmed.
- If this is an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the assessment must be completed within 30 days of the entity becoming aware of grounds to suspect a breach. The data room is dated 22 September 2026 and today is 5 November 2026. **The assessment period may already have run.** Wattlebridge should ask immediately when the company became aware and what assessment and notification steps have been taken.
- Pushback: require a forensic review of access logs, confirmation of NDB assessment and notification status, a specific privacy warranty, and a **special indemnity** for all costs, regulatory penalties, notification costs and third-party claims. This indemnity should sit outside the cap, de minimis, basket and time limits, with a dedicated escrow or retention until the matter is closed.
- Clause 1.4 says nothing admits that notification is "legally required." That should not stop Wattlebridge from requiring a definitive position before signing.

### 2. Riverlark facility (AUD ~3.2m) and security

- The Seller proposes a release "following Completion." That is backwards. In a debt-free/cash-free deal the facility should be repaid at Completion from the price, with a payoff letter, and the Seller should deliver the discharge of security (including any PPSR registrations) at Completion.
- Pushback: require a payoff letter with an exact figure, a funds-flow payment direct to Riverlark, and delivery of all discharges and PPSR removals at Completion. Any shortfall should reduce the price, not be carried by Wattlebridge. The release should not be a post-Completion deliverable.

### 3. Bluefen change-control consent (~30% of revenue)

- The consent is not in the data room. Clause 11.3 conditions have not been shown as satisfied. The Seller proposes to treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of "the counterparty's written consent" and to use only "reasonable endeavours."
- Pushback: make the consent, in agreed form and without adverse variation, a **condition precedent** to Completion. Conditions in clause 11.3 must also be satisfied, not just consent delivered. Any cost or fee to obtain consent should be borne by the Seller. If consent is not obtained, Wattlebridge should have a walk-away right, and the price should be reduced or held back if the consent comes with commercial concessions. Add a specific indemnity for loss of Bluefen revenue if the contract is terminated or varied due to the change of control within a defined period.

### 4. Ironquay IP and SOW3 (AUD 180k open)

- Under DD-004 clause 7.3, transfer of SOW3 project materials depends on payment of every SOW3 fee. About AUD 180k is recorded as open, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- The Seller's indemnity is "limited to the specific SOW3 payment." That is too narrow. The indemnity should cover all Ironquay ownership, title and third-party IP claims, not only the SOW3 fee.
- Pushback: the Seller should pay the AUD 180k before Completion (or it should be deducted from the price), and deliver a confirmatory assignment of all project materials. Add a special IP indemnity outside the general caps and time limits, and confirm there are no other open SOWs.

### 5. Employee completion bonuses (AUD 420k)

- These are conditional on Completion and continued employment, but they are not in the draft funds flow. The disclosure does not say whether payroll tax or superannuation on-costs apply.
- Completion-triggered bonuses are typically a Seller cost. They should be treated as a debt-like item and deducted from the price, with the Seller bearing all related payroll tax and superannuation.
- Pushback: add them to the funds flow as Seller-funded, and require confirmation of the on-cost calculation. Any retention bonuses that Wattlebridge wants for continuity should be a separate Buyer decision, not an inherited Seller cost.

### 6. Liability cap, thresholds and time limits

- **Cap:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general warranties is well below market for a deal of this type. Pushback: general warranty cap at or near 100% of price, or at least materially higher than 20%.
- **Fundamental warranties:** the Seller's proposal to apply the general cap and time limits to title and capacity is unacceptable. Title and capacity should be capped at the full price, with a longer claims period.
- **De minimis and basket:** AUD 25k de minimis is high for a deal this size, and the basket is structured as a deductible (only the excess is recoverable). Pushback: lower de minimis (for example AUD 10k), aggregation of related claims, and a **tipping basket** so that once the threshold is crossed, the claim is recoverable from the first dollar.
- **Time limits:** 18 months is short. Pushback: 24 to 36 months for general warranties, a longer period for fundamental warranties (consistent with the limitation periods under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW) for contractual claims), and a tax period that runs until the ATO amendment period has expired. The Seller's proposal that "any limitation applies to all Claims" should be rejected.

### 7. Tax and IP warranties

- The Seller treats tax and IP as "settled under the general regime." That is not acceptable. Pre-Completion tax liabilities should be covered by a **standalone tax indemnity**, with first-dollar recovery, outside the general cap and basket. IP warranties should be separately negotiated, with an appropriate cap.

### 8. General disclosure, buyer knowledge and exclusive remedy

- **Clause 1.1 and 1.2:** the whole data room and public registers are deemed disclosed. This would neutralise nearly every warranty. Reject. Disclosure should be specific, against a specific warranty, and fairly disclosed.
- **Clause 8.3:** claims are excluded for anything known to Wattlebridge or its advisers, including anything "discoverable" from the data room. This is an anti-sandbagging clause. Pushback: pro-sandbagging wording so Wattlebridge's knowledge does not defeat a claim. Under Australian law the position on knowledge and warranty claims is not fully settled, so the clause must be express. Known issues should instead be dealt with through special indemnities and price, not through the knowledge exclusion.
- **Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5:** exclusive remedy, limitations and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature." Reject as drafted. Carve-outs should include fraud and wilful concealment (which cannot be contracted out of in any event), equitable remedies, specific performance, and indemnity claims.

### 9. Consents and assignment (lease and Mossvale)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** the notification obligation may be a precursor to landlord consent. Require a written landlord confirmation that the share sale does not require consent, or that consent has been given, and confirm no default under the lease.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** the restriction on assignment does not, on the record, require consent for a share sale. Require a legal confirmation or Mossvale's written acknowledgement that no change-of-control consent is required.

### 10. Supplier renewals (AUD 330k)

- Three related renewals of AUD 110k each. The Seller calls them ordinary course, but the disclosure does not say whether they are terminable, multi-year, or accrued. Splitting renewals of this size can also indicate that the contracts are linked.
- Pushback: obtain the full terms, confirm whether any are outside the ordinary course or pre-committed, and treat any pre-Completion liabilities as debt-like or working-capital items.

### 11. Title (DD-012)

- The share register shows Harbourglass as holder of 100%. That is a starting point, not verification. Require executed share transfers, original certificates if any, an ASIC extract, PPSR searches on the shares, and confirmation of no options or other encumbrances. Confirm any constitutional transfer restrictions or pre-emption rights have been met.

### 12. Price mechanics and funds flow

- The Seller says the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics," but the deal documents do not state whether the price is adjusted by completion accounts or locked box. If it is locked box, there must be a leakage indemnity. If completion accounts, there must be a working-capital adjustment.
- Pushback: require a complete funds flow showing the price, Riverlark payoff, bonuses, the Ironquay holdback, any escrow or retention, and transaction costs.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| Priority | Issue | Key pushback |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Privacy incident (DD-006) | Confirm NDB status now; forensic review; special indemnity outside caps; dedicated escrow |
| 2 | Riverlark (~AUD 3.2m) | Repay at Completion from the price; discharges delivered at Completion |
| 3 | Bluefen consent (~30% revenue) | Consent and cl. 11.3 conditions as CP; Seller bears cost; walk-away right; revenue-loss indemnity |
| 4 | Ironquay / SOW3 (AUD 180k) | Pay before Completion or deduct; confirmatory assignment; broad IP special indemnity |
| 5 | Bonuses (AUD 420k) | Seller-funded debt-like deduction; Seller bears on-costs |
| 6 | Cap, basket, time limits | Cap near 100%; fundamental warranties at full price; tipping basket; 24–36 months; tax to ATO period |
| 7 | Tax and IP | Standalone tax indemnity, first-dollar; separate IP warranties |
| 8 | General disclosure, cl. 8.3, exclusive remedy | Specific disclosure only; pro-sandbagging; carve-outs for fraud and equitable relief |
| 9 | Lease and Mossvale consents | Written landlord and Mossvale confirmations |
| 10 | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | Full terms; treat pre-Completion commitments as debt-like |
| 11 | Title | Executed transfers; ASIC and PPSR searches; encumbrance warranty |
| 12 | Price mechanics | Clarify completion accounts or locked box; full funds flow |

**Next steps:** First, ask the Seller for the privacy assessment timeline and status. Second, put the Riverlark and Bluefen conditions into the next mark-up as conditions precedent. Third, prepare a special indemnity and escrow schedule covering the privacy, Ironquay, bonus, supplier and tax items, so they sit outside the general regime. Finally, consider whether a buyer-side W&I policy is viable, bearing in mind that known matters such as these will almost certainly be excluded from cover and must be handled through specific indemnities.
